explain.say: Look around you. A spoon, a glass of water, the air you breathe. Everything is made of stuff called matter, and matter comes in three main kinds: solid, liquid and gas. Let's sort, then zoom in to see why they are different.

explain.say: Now look! Here it is in 3D: solid, liquid and gas. Can you see the solid and the liquid? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.

draw.text: Solid, liquid or gas? Sorting things around you

explain.say: Here are the tiny bits inside a solid, called particles, far too small to see. See how they are packed tight in rows, just wiggling in place? That is why a solid, like a rock or a spoon, keeps its own shape. Can you squash a spoon with your fingers?

Now the particles of a liquid. They are still close, but they slide and tumble past each other. So a liquid flows and takes the shape of whatever holds it, a cup, a bottle or a puddle. What happens when you pour juice into a tall glass?

And here are gas particles, zooming far apart in every direction. So a gas spreads out to fill any space, like the smell of fresh chapatis filling the whole house. Air is a gas you cannot see. Can you feel it when you blow on your hand?

Back to sorting: see the Liquids group light up, with water. Here is the magic: water can be all three! Freeze it and it is solid ice, heat it and it becomes steam, a gas. Super job, scientist! Wow fact: honey and toothpaste flow slowly, but they are still liquids.

faq.q: What is the difference between a solid, a liquid and a gas?
faq.a: A solid keeps its shape, because its particles are packed tight. A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container, because its particles slide past each other. A gas spreads out to fill any space, because its particles are far apart.
asks: What are the three states of matter?

faq.a: A solid is matter that keeps its own shape and size, like ice, wood, a rock or a spoon. Its particles are packed tightly and only wiggle in place.

faq.q: Why does a liquid take the shape of its container?
faq.a: The particles in a liquid stay close together but can slide over each other, so the liquid flows to fill the bottom of whatever it is in.
Yes. Air is a mixture of gases, mostly nitrogen and oxygen. We cannot see it, but we feel it as wind and need it to breathe.

faq.q: Can water be a solid, a liquid and a gas?
faq.a: Yes. Water is a solid when frozen into ice, a liquid in a glass, and a gas called water vapour or steam when heated.
asks: What are the three forms of water?

facts: Air is about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen.
Water is unusual: we meet it every day as a solid (ice), a liquid and a gas (water vapour).

quiz.say: Which of these is a gas?
quiz.why: Steam is water as a gas.
